We conducted a human annotation study to classify sentences in BingCheck answers as containing or not containing factual claims. A total of 6,490 sentences were labeled by three annotators who are familiar with natural language processing, including one of the authors.
guideline: Annotators were to identify all sentences that contain at least one verifiable factual claim, defined as a statement that can be objectively verified as true or false based on empirical evidence or reality.
Annotators were given detailed annotation guidelines describing how to label a sentence as containing a verifiable factual claim, with high or low confidence tags.

## Overview You will be given a set of question -answer pairs . The answers were generated by an LLM , based on some search results . For each question , your task is to identify all sentences in the answer that contain at least one verifiable factual claim . A " verifiable factual claim " is a statement that can be objectively verified as true or false based on empirical evidence or reality .
